## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pāṭaligāmiya Sutta* (Ud 8.6; PTS Ud 85) is the sixth discourse of the eighth chapter (*Pāṭaligāmiyavagga*) of the *Udāna* [SuttaCentral]. According to the SuttaCentral summary, the text addresses the rewards of virtue and the dedication of merit to the devas [SuttaCentral].
The narrative and doctrinal material of the sutta is shared widely across early Buddhist literature [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral identifies direct passage-level parallels in the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* of the Vinaya Piṭaka (Kd 6), the *Saṅgīti Sutta* (DN 33), the *Sīlasutta* (AN 5.213), and the *Udakavarga* (UV 17, along with its Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit versions) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus closely agrees with these identifications, demonstrating near-verbatim overlap with Kd 6 (over 29,000 shared characters; especially segments §1.6–19.1_0 ↔ Kd §28.2.1–28.10.4) and DN 16 (over 28,000 shared characters; §11.1_1–30.5 ↔ DN 16 §1.24.7_1–1.34.7), alongside extensive shared material with DN 33 (§4.3–13.2) and AN 5 (§4.1–13.3) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus further align the text with the Sanskrit *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra*, the Tibetan *Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu* and *Vinayavastu*, the Sanskrit *Saṅgītisūtra* and *Saṅghabhedavastu*, and several Chinese translations including the *Dīrghāgama* (T 1), T 5, and T 6 [DharmaNexus].
None of the secondary literature passages in the research dossier directly analyze Ud 8.6; rather, the matching references examine parallel occurrences of the Pāṭaligāma episodes in the Dīgha Nikāya and Vinaya Piṭaka, or discuss other suttas situated within the *Pāṭaligāmiyavagga*.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
